summary: MARS PATH is an interactive geospatial application designed to support human exploration planning on Mars. It integrates scientific data from multiple NASA missions into a layered map of a selected Martian region, combining topography, high-resolution imagery, thermal information, and geological and mineralogical observations. The platform enables users to examine terrain conditions, identify potential hazards, locate scientific points of interest, and plan exploration routes. By bringing distributed planetary science data into a unified interface, MARS PATH aims to make Martian surface information more accessible and useful for planning safer, science-driven human exploration missions.
details:
Project Overview

MARS PATH is a scientific mapping and route-planning application designed to support future human surface exploration on Mars.

The project addresses the challenge of fragmented planetary science information. Data collected by different NASA missions and instruments provide valuable information about Martian terrain, geology, thermal properties, and surface conditions, but these datasets are not always accessible together in a single operational view.

How It Works

The application brings together multiple scientific data layers within an interactive map focused on a selected Martian exploration region.

Users will be able to:

  • Explore the Martian surface through geographic and scientific layers.
  • Examine elevation and terrain characteristics to identify potentially difficult areas.
  • Visualize orbital imagery and available surface observations.
  • Identify geological and mineralogical features relevant to scientific investigation.
  • Mark exploration destinations and plan a route connecting selected points of interest.
  • Review relevant environmental and terrain information associated with the planned route.

Scientific Foundation

The project uses publicly available NASA planetary science data, combining observations from different missions and instruments. Each data layer will include its source and relevant technical context.

The initial implementation focuses on a geographically defined area where complementary NASA observations are available.

Expected Benefits and Impact

MARS PATH aims to reduce the fragmentation of planetary data by translating scientific observations into a unified geospatial interface.

Its intended impact is to support exploration planning, improve access to scientific context, help identify terrain-related challenges, and connect scientific investigation with route planning.

The application may also serve as an educational and research resource for understanding the challenges of future human exploration of Mars.

Technology and Development

The project is being designed as a browser-based application using geospatial visualization, digital mapping, scientific data integration, and interactive route-planning components.

NASA data products and their metadata will be documented to support transparency and reproducibility.

Innovation

The central contribution of MARS PATH is the integration of scientific mapping and exploration planning into one interface. Instead of presenting isolated planetary datasets, the application connects terrain interpretation, scientific targets, and route planning within the same geographic context.

The project distinguishes observed scientific data from derived analyses and modeled route assessments.
